claims.text: Landau-Devonshire theory can determine whether an HEA has a ferromagnetic ground state.
First-principles calculations can determine whether an HEA has a ferromagnetic ground state.
The HEAs under consideration can have FCC or BCC structures.
An external magnetic field is an intervention for assessing ferromagnetic ground states in HEAs.
Temperature variation can be used to assess the magnetic state of an HEA.
The relevant temperature range is 0 K to 1000 K.
The relevant magnetic-field range extends to 10 T.
Crystal structure is a mediator of the HEA's magnetic properties.
Atomic arrangement, defects, and impurities mediate the HEA's magnetic behavior.
Landau-Devonshire theory and first-principles calculations determine the magnetic properties of the HEA.
The presence or absence of a ferromagnetic ground state depends on HEA composition.
The presence or absence of ferromagnetism depends on temperature.
The presence or absence of ferromagnetism depends on magnetic-field strength.
The baseline is the HEA's magnetic behavior without an applied magnetic field or temperature variation.
Outside the stated temperature and magnetic-field ranges, the HEA exhibits non-ferromagnetic behavior.
Structural complexity and limitations of the theoretical models create uncertainty in predicting ferromagnetic ground states.
X-ray diffraction, neutron scattering, and first-principles calculations can jointly test the hypothesis.
Magnetic susceptibility, magnetization curves, and crystal-structure determination are the proposed experimental observables.
A mismatch between experimental results and predicted magnetic properties would negate the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis asks about a ground state, ordinarily a zero-temperature property, but the predicted ground-state outcome is described as depending on temperatures as high as 1000 K without distinguishing the ground state from finite-temperature magnetic phases.
